data.turoyo: Fayəš arbʕo əšne bayn aǧ ǧən, kle zalṭono, mkasyo i lašayḏe bu pərč, kmazheri ʕayne bayn u pərč, gzoyəʕ ḥa mene.
data.translation: Vier Jahre blieb er so in nacktem Zustande unter den Geistern; sein ganzer Körper bedeckte sich mit Haren, und nur seine Augen funkelten aus denselben hervor, so dass man sich vor ihm hätte fürchten können.

rationale: Thin Infectum sense-1 cell: a full human-eye context beside the inherited cat-eye example; the eyes are the subject, with no gaze target.

summary: kmazheri agrees with plural ʕayne; bayn u pərč is a location. The fear reaction gzoyəʕ ḥa mene describes the observer's response and does not supply an object for sense 2.
The inherited Infectum example is unnumbered but illustrates sense 1 by its intransitive cat-eye subject. No restructuring of it is needed.
PrS 30/17 appears in an inherited note, while the supplied occurrence is labelled PrS 15/6. The available record does not establish which numbering system or verse offset is correct.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. The love object and u ʕəlmo kule aḏəʕla support making something known in the Turoyo, but not an established connection to sparkle or angry staring.
The source is unprefixed zhərxu with an apparent second-person plural agent. The absence of inherited III ma- is not sufficient to identify a native I paradigm or reconstruct its base forms.
Arabic ẓhr manifestation is a reader’s contact hypothesis; it must not be silently equated with the entry’s Arabic zhr shining etymology. No etymological correction or new stem is published.
Read-only form lookup returns zhr as a consonantal candidate, not proof of lexical identity. Search offenbar located other manifestation verbs but no matching zhərxu paradigm.
Round-1 III.1 sparkle and III.2 gaze distinctions are retained. The new manifestation context is neither proof of another participant type for sparkle nor grounds for moving an existing example.
Collate supplied PrS 15/6, inherited + PrS 30/17 and the reader-reported parallel reference PrS 30/18 before correcting citations.
Identify the root and stem of zhərxu from the recording or a speaker. Is it contact material related to Arabic ẓhr, a reduced III, or an I formation?
Supply standalone Preterit and Infectum forms before creating a new manifestation stem or homonym under this spelling.
Human eyes glitter through body hair, beside inherited cat eyes. A frightening appearance does not turn this into transitive angry staring.
